items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: I just hired Tom and I had a boy named Buddy Collins, who was a singer. And he started a fight in the auditorium that night of free-for-all.

ctx.x: What about Thomasville? Do you mind talking about that?

No, no. The reason for that is I had Tom Johnson in the band from here. I just hired Tom and I had a boy named Buddy Collins, who was a singer. And he started a fight in the auditorium that night of free-for-all. And I was on the front door with the principal of the school, taking care of the business and the money. They hurdled a whole band off in a paddy wagon, two girls I had that were dancers, the James sisters. Put them all in there. Of course, a few of the fellas got away. Mickey and I think it was Kato and…
The demand wasn't involved in the fight or anything?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: Another fellow, Buddy Collins. He was from here.

ctx.x: What about if a guy got sick? And you're on the road.

That's another question. It's hard for me to answer. I don't remember anybody getting sick, but one time was Turner, wasn't it? What about that? Well, that was in later years. But Henry Turner got real sick in a little town of Ashland, Kentucky, I think. It was in the hills. And we had to...no, I'm sorry. Another fellow, Buddy Collins. He was from here. I don't know if you ever hear any talk about him. He was a vocalist. You've told me about him. Yeah. Well, Nick Turner got sick in this little small town in the…
I don't know if he's still going or not. You were going to say something?
